title: Wangari and the Little Green Tree
globalStyle: This is an English reader's theater for young elementary school students in Taiwan. Speak clearly and a little slowly, with natural, expressive storytelling intonation so children can follow and imitate.

narrator.label: Narrator
narrator.style: You are a warm, calm storyteller reading a picture book aloud to children.

wangari.label: Wangari
wangari.style: You are Wangari, a bright, curious and determined young Kenyan girl who loves trees. Sound youthful, sincere and full of energy.

mama.label: Mama
mama.style: You are Wangari's loving, gentle and wise mother. Sound warm, kind and encouraging.

friend.label: Friend
friend.style: You are Wangari's friend, a lively young villager. Sound friendly and expressive, sometimes worried or doubtful, later amazed and proud.

trees.label: Trees
trees.style: You are the voice of the trees: deep, slow, magical and grand, like an ancient forest speaking with joy.

chorus.label: All
chorus.style: You are one of a group of children shouting this line together on stage, loud, happy and energetic.

scenes.title: Scene 1 — A Girl Who Loved Trees
scenes.titleZh: 場景一：喜歡樹木的女孩

lines.text: Long ago, in Kenya, Africa, there was a little girl named Wangari.
Wangari, look at the trees. They are big and strong.
Yes, Mama! Trees give us shade. Trees give us fruit. Trees give birds a home.
lines.tone: Happy and proud, listing each thing.

lines.text: We love trees! Trees are our friends!
Wangari loved nature. She loved learning, too.
I want to learn. I want to help people.
Wangari grew up. She studied science and became a teacher. One day, she went back to the villages in Kenya.
Oh, no! Where are the trees?
People need wood for cooking. The forests are getting smaller.
The soil is dry. The water is harder to find.

lines.tone: Thinking for a moment, then suddenly bright and excited.

lines.text: Yes! One tree can help. Two trees can help. Many trees can help even more!
Plant a tree! Help the Earth!

scenes.title: Scene 3 — One Small Seed
scenes.titleZh: 場景三：一顆小小的種子

lines.text: Wangari and many women began to plant trees.
Can one little seed really help?
Dig, dig, dig! Plant, plant, plant! Water, water, water!
The women planted more and more trees. The little trees grew. The people had more trees, more shade, and more hope.
One tree! Two trees! Three trees!
Yes. One seed. One tree. One person.
lines.tone: Slow and meaningful, with a pause after each part.

lines.text: More and more people joined Wangari. They planted millions of trees in Kenya.
Green trees! Green Earth! Green hope!
Wangari never stopped helping people and the Earth. In 2004, she received the Nobel Peace Prize. She was the first African woman to receive the prize.
You started with one small idea.
Can grow into a big tree!
Wangari taught the world something very important. We do not need to be big to make a difference. We can start with one small thing.
What can you do for the Earth?
We can plant! We can care! We can help!
One person can make a difference!
